summary.headline: MAS Financial Q4 FY26 consolidated PAT rose 25% YoY to INR104 crore, with AUM at INR15,304 crore, up 19%.
summary.overview: Consolidated PAT for Q4 FY26 was INR104 crore versus INR83 crore a year earlier, and full-year PAT was INR379 crore, up 21%. Standalone AUM grew 18.71% and standalone PAT grew 23.39% YoY in the quarter to around INR100 crore. Standalone net Stage 3 was 1.70%, slightly better than 1.72% in December 2025, while gross Stage 3 edged up to 2.57% from 2.56%. Cost of borrowing fell 42 bps YoY to 9.39%, and management guided to 9.20-9.25% over the next two to three quarters. Credit cost was elevated because of deliberate aggressive write-offs of 90+ DPD assets, which management said were funded from profit.

segments.name: Standalone MFSL - Micro-enterprise loans (MEL)
segments.commentary: AUM rose about 20% to INR5,737 crore from INR4,793 crore.

segments.name: Standalone MFSL - SME loans
segments.commentary: AUM grew 15.78% to INR5,213 crore from INR4,502 crore.

segments.name: Standalone MFSL - Two-wheeler
segments.commentary: AUM grew 35.43% to INR1,063 crore from INR785 crore; yields cited at 19-23%.

segments.name: Standalone MFSL - Commercial vehicle
segments.commentary: AUM grew 11% to INR1,085 crore from INR979 crore; growth being deliberately slowed for 1-2 quarters.

segments.name: Standalone MFSL - Salaried personal loan
segments.commentary: AUM grew around 22% to INR1,264 crore from INR1,040 crore.

segments.name: Housing finance subsidiary
segments.commentary: AUM rose 22.41% to INR940 crore from INR768 crore; Q4 PAT INR3.70 crore vs INR2.64 crore, net Stage 3 0.68%. Management aims for INR1,000 crore, now about a quarter later than planned.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth guided at 20-25% on a sustained basis; long-term target of INR1 lakh crore AUM by 2036.
Credit cost guided at 1-1.25% of closing AUM statistically, with management indicating about 1.25-1.3% on closing AUM, and up to about 1.5% in quarters with aggressive write-offs.
Cost-to-NII guided at 35-37%; ROA after opex and credit cost targeted at 2.75-3%.
Yield range-bound at 16-17%, expected to be sustained into FY27.
Cost of borrowing guided to fall from 9.39% to around 9.20-9.25% over the next 2-3 quarters.
Branch additions of 30-35 planned in FY27 after a year of consolidating existing branches.
Dividend: final dividend INR0.75 per share, total INR2 per share for FY26, about 10% payout.
Capital adequacy to be maintained at around 20%; debt tie-up for about half of FY27 done, full-year tie-up expected soon.
capex_capacity: More than 200 branches and about 16,500 centres; branch network to grow by 30-35 in FY27.
Average cash and cash equivalent balance of about INR1,000 crore plus unutilised cash credit of over INR200 crore.
Cash credit facility of about INR1,500 crore across 14 banks, utilised at 70-75%.
Sanctioned facilities over INR2,000 crore as of 31 March (term loans, NCDs, direct assignment, co-lending).
Term loan sanctioned pipeline of about INR1,300 crore; INR750 crore term loan raised in Q4 at 3-5 year tenor; INR100 crore NCDs raised in Q4.
Direct assignment of INR940 crore executed in Q4; a further INR500 crore+ of direct assignment and co-lending sanctions to be used in the current quarter.
demand_pricing: Direct sourcing is about 64% of the book; fintech partnerships are about 10% of business.
Yield rose about 40 bps sequentially, attributed to fintech mix and 2-wheeler growth; SME yields were also higher.
Management said assignment income is amortised, not upfront, and the NII rise was mainly from lower borrowing cost and the MCLR reset.
Standalone 90+ write-offs were aggressive in FY26 (more than 0.10% of assets), mostly unsecured per management.
Caution list added petrol pumps, gas agencies, transporters and some chemical industries in Feb-March 2026, alongside textile and agro, due to West Asia supply concerns.
Management reported no slowdown in disbursement growth as of the call.

qa_highlights.question: How is MAS using data and AI for risk-adjusted growth, and what early warning systems exist?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it back-tests risk models on its own repayment experience, not generic bureau scores; it moved from LOS to business rule engines and plans AI-based risk management after 6-9 months. Field checks included more than 2,000-3,000 commercial vehicle borrowers after the Middle East crisis, plus bounce data from 100% bank or e-NACH collections.

qa_highlights.question: Will the West Asia crisis and inflation affect lending and asset quality?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said asset quality should hold but is being watched closely; it is growing CV more slowly as an energy- and logistics-linked precaution. Disbursement growth has not slowed.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for cost of borrowing and the Q4 cost of borrowing trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost of borrowing is 9.39% and is expected to fall to 9.20-9.25% over 2-3 quarters. Q4 interest expense was about INR222 crore vs INR219 crore in Q3, with the MCLR reset adding to NII.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the origination and fee cost high, and what is driving opex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the fees and commission depend on product structure. Fintech partners get the spread as commission, and yields rose about 0.5%. Opex is judged against ROA, not in isolation.

qa_highlights.question: Why did credit cost rise and what is the normalised level?
qa_highlights.answer: The rise was from deliberate write-offs of 90+ DPD assets, not stress. Normal credit cost is 1-1.25% of closing AUM; 1.5% is possible in quarters with aggressive write-offs.

qa_highlights.question: Why is CV growth slow, and what is the write-off and recovery policy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is slowing CV growth for 1-2 quarters due to logistics and transport risk. Write-offs occur after 360 days across all products; recoveries are credited to P&L net.

risks_watch: Rising inflation and energy costs from the West Asia crisis could hit logistics, transport and fuel-linked MSMEs.
Credit cost is a function of aggressive write-off policy; quarterly credit costs could run towards 1.5%.
Pricing may need to be passed on to borrowers if borrowing costs fall, which could compress the yield gain.
Housing finance subsidiary's INR1,000 crore AUM target now slips about a quarter.
Debt tie-up for FY27 is only about half complete; rate reduction depends on market conditions.
Gross Stage 3 is at 2.57%, up slightly QoQ.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and profitability, with a clear 20-25% AUM growth target. Cautious on the macro, with CV growth slowed and sector caution lists expanded. Management was less direct on the split of NII growth and on the detail of the write-off strategy.
key_quotes: And on the asset side, we continue to have the confidence to grow anywhere between 20% to 25%, given the positive macro situation because we always prioritize risk management and profitability over just the growth.
So, we are at a striking distance away from INR1,000 crores.
We have cash credit facility of approximately INR1500 crore spread over 14 banks, of which we maintain utilization level of around 70 %-75%, keeping the remaining portion as liquidity buffer.
So, we do not upfront income in order to improve the profitability or the NII growth.

adds.what: 30-35 new branches planned in FY27 after a year of consolidating existing branches
Housing finance subsidiary AUM target of INR1,000 crore (about a quarter later than planned)

growth.why: Management reiterated AUM growth of 20-25% on a sustained basis (long-term INR1 lakh crore AUM by 2036), backed partly by 30-35 branch additions in FY27, INR940 crore direct assignment done in Q4 and INR500 crore+ more assignment/co-lending sanctions for the current quarter, plus a INR1,300 crore term loan pipeline; no capacity utilisation figure was given.
